text:
maya: Heads up, I'm seeing packet loss spikes and elevated reconnects from nodes in us-west-2b, GPU task failures ~5% over the last 8m :rotating_light:
oncall-bot: ALERT: network.anomaly detected in region us-west-2b (host-group: gpu-pool-b). Severity: warning. Link: https://monitoring.internal/alerts/12345
sam: copying logs, can you paste the top error lines?
maya: paste: `2026-03-18T18:02:11Z kernel: rcv error: rx timeout` and `kubelet: liveness probe failed for pod gpu-infer-xyz`
liam: confirming, I see elevated TCP retransmits at the TORs for that AZ, looks like intermittent egress saturation.
nina: Are we seeing any infra autoscaler activity? Any new launches failing?
maya: ASG scaled fine but several instances stuck in NotReady for >3m. We had to restart one kube-proxy to restore node heartbeat.
ops-sre: recommendation: cordon the AZ and perform tenant-aware drains while we assess network fabric. Prefer not to full-evac unless we see degradation >15% or customer impact.
sam: agree. Plan: 1) cordon us-west-2b GPUs 2) reroute new placements off the AZ 3) gentle drain with keep-warm tag for warm caches 4) monitor tail latency + pod restarts
liam: cost note — if we rehome heavy batches to us-east-1 right away, inter-region egress will bump monthly infra by ~18-25% this week for heavy customers. We should prefer intra-region fallback to us-west-2a/c if capacity exists.
maya: running cordon command on the GPU node pool: 
```
kubectl label nodes -l pool=gpu-usw2b cordoned_by=oncall-1918
kubectl cordon node-0a1b2c
```
ops-sre: start tenant-aware drain: use the script that honors `keep-warm: true` and maintains 1 replica of customer-critical fleets. Command: 
```
./tools/drain-tenants --pool gpu-usw2b --graceful 600 --keep-warm-label keep-warm=true
```
liam: I'll open a quick capacity window in us-west-2a/c by bumping the instance cap + trigger preemptible burst pool. Watch quotas.
nina: pinging CS: @cs-pager — please flag top 3 Dedicated customers on hostnames that might observe latency spikes so we can notify them proactively.
cs-pager: got it, compiling list now. Will DM the list and send an email if we exceed 5% error rate per customer.
maya: drain running, first batch of pods being rescheduled. Prefetch/cache-warm triggered for embeddings cache. Seeing pod start delays ~45s, acceptable.
sam: good. Can someone add routing override rule to prefer us-west-2a/c in the router policy v2? small change: weight 0 for 2b pools.
ops-sre: making change: `routectl set-weight --pool gpu-usw2b=0 --region us-west-2` (rolling).
oncall-bot: DEPLOY: routectl change in progress by ops-sre.
liam: watch metrics: token latency and model response 95p. If 95p degrades >200ms for 3 consecutive mins we escalate to full evac.
maya: note: one Dedicated tenant's batch job hit retry loop, I paused it via the control plane and set fallback to local model variant.
ops-sre: timeline: cordon at T+2m, gentle-drain in waves (10% of tenants every 60s), monitor for customer-visible errors. If everything stays stable we keep cordon + partial drain for 1-2 hours to let routing propagate.
sam: logging this in incident tracker and pinging product for status page blurb. Command to create incident: `incidentctl new --sev=3 --component=gpu-pool-usw2b --owner=eng-oncall`
liam: one more risk: if fabric flaps again, some nodes may lose NVLINK fabric metrics; be ready to fallback to CPU-only small instances for low-priority training workloads.
nina: copying notes to the runbook and tagging `followup: postmortem` for root cause analysis.
maya: current status: cordoned, 40% of tenant pods migrated, tail latency stable so far. I'll keep updates every 5m. :thumbsup:
cs-pager: emailed customers on the list with a heads-up and mitigation steps.
ops-sre: continuing to watch network counters + orchestration events. If anyone sees an unexplained 5xx spike call +1 on pager.
sam: thanks all — keeping this thread for decisions and next steps.
